_README: TEMPLATE. Copy to courses/<your-slug>/course.json, replace every value, then follow
PIPELINE.md. courses/ is gitignored, so your course data stays local and is never pushed.
The numbers in 'holes' and 'tees' are FACTS from the club's published scorecard -- transcribe
them, do not estimate. Cross-check against a second source: aggregator sites swap the nines,
misstate par, and (seen in practice) list a WOMEN'S rating in a men's column. Leave a value
null rather than guess; the book prints an em-dash for null.
Keys the engine actually reads are marked REQUIRED / OPTIONAL below. Any key starting with
an underscore is ignored, so this block is safe to keep.
name: Example Golf Club
_location: REQUIRED. Two jobs, and the second one is easy to get wrong:
1. picks the NAD83 UTM zone for the LiDAR reprojection (26900 + zone);
2. tells YOUR course's holes apart from a neighbouring course's. OSM often has two clubs, or
two 18s of one club, inside one query box with the same hole numbers 1-18. geo.hole_lines
picks the way nearest this point and REFUSES when the margin is under 150 m.
So at a 36-hole club, do NOT put the shared clubhouse address in both course.json files: give each
course a point inside ITS OWN routing. Castlewood's two courses share one street address and their
location values sit 960 m apart for exactly this reason, which buys a ~600 m margin. Set both to the
clubhouse and the nearer course wins BOTH books -- it resolves silently, and you get another course's
holes, greens and slope printed on your cards with no error at all.
_par: OPTIONAL, defaults 72. Must equal the sum of the per-hole pars; a test checks this.
_tees: REQUIRED for the Tees panel. yards/rating/slope come from the card; use null for anything the
club does not publish (9-hole courses often have no rating). Ratings must FALL as yardage
falls -- if they don't, you have mixed a women's rating into a men's column.
_featured_tee: REQUIRED: the big number on each hole card. secondary_tee is the small one.
_shorter_tee_is_deliberate: OPTIONAL: set true only if this book is meant for a tee that is NOT the longest column
on the scorecard -- e.g. a forward-tee junior edition. Without it the build prints a
loud NOTE, because every derived number (tee marker, from-tee yardages, carries,
elevation) is measured from the headline tee, so a wrong one misstates the hole all day.
_hole_cols: REQUIRED. Describes each row in 'holes': always par, then mens_hcp, then one entry per tee
whose yardages you list. The tee names here must appear in 'tees' above.
_holes: REQUIRED. hole number -> [par, mens_hcp, <one yardage per tee in hole_cols order>].
mens_hcp must be a permutation of 1..N. Per-tee yardages must sum to that tee's total.
A 9-hole course simply lists 1..9; the engine adapts (single Total row, no front/back split).
_osm_bbox: REQUIRED: [south, west, north, east] enclosing the whole property, with a little margin.
Too tight is a real trap -- a green just outside the box looks 'missing from OSM' and tempts
you into hand-digitising geometry that already exists. Widen the box first.
_build_mode: OPTIONAL, defaults 'full'. Set to 'yardage' when no trustworthy post-construction elevation
exists (e.g. the course was rebuilt after the latest public LiDAR flight): the book then
prints verified yardages with BLANK greens to mark your own read, instead of slope maps that
_greens_possibly_outdated: OPTIONAL: hole numbers whose greens were rebuilt AFTER the LiDAR flight. Those cards print
the real map but are labelled 'pre-rebuild data' and the guide page names the holes.
If you set this you MUST also set greens_outdated_basis (below): the claim is about real
cards, so the evidence for it has to be recorded. The test suite enforces that pairing.
_greens_outdated_basis: REQUIRED whenever greens_possibly_outdated is set: how you know, in one sentence, with
a source. It is reproduced in legal/03_PROVENANCE_BY_COURSE.md beside the caveat it
justifies, so a reader can audit the claim instead of taking it on trust.
e.g. 'Phased Flynn restoration; front nine reopened 2024 (club newsletter, Mar 2024).'
_dem_source: RECOMMENDED: a human label for where the elevation came from, e.g.
'USGS 3DEP LiDAR, CA Alameda County 2021, 0.4 m'. The provenance table prefers the real
project name decoded from the LAZ filenames on disk and falls back to this when those
tiles carry no project in their name -- and says which it used.
_lidar_flown: WRITTEN FOR YOU by tools/lidar_dates.py --write, which decodes the true acquisition date from
the LAZ point records. Do not hand-edit. A USGS project NAME is not a flight date: four of our
courses were mislabelled by 2-12 years until this was measured.
_lidar_crs: OPTIONAL override, e.g. 'EPSG:2227', when a LAZ header carries no readable CRS.
_tz: OPTIONAL: IANA zone, e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'. Only affects the LiDAR FLIGHT DATE,
which tools/lidar_dates.py decodes from GPS time and reports as a local day so it can
be checked against a flight log. The zone is inferred from a CONUS longitude band,
which is exact for every course here and wrong only near a boundary or outside the US.
_card: OPTIONAL {w,h,page_w,page_h} inches. Defaults 3.5 x 5.0 on US Letter (4-up duplex).
_sources: STRONGLY RECOMMENDED and free-text. Record exactly where each number came from and what you
could NOT verify. This is the project's provenance record; write it as if a stranger will audit it.

sources.scorecard: Where the par/handicap/yardages came from, which sources agreed, and anything single-source or unverified.
sources.elevation: USGS 3DEP LiDAR (public domain) — name the project, and note any caveat (e.g. flown mid-renovation).
